channelTitle: Forget the fancy collagen powder, Grandma June just simmered bones on the stove
hook: Forget the fancy collagen powder, this is what grandmothers were already simmering on the back burner for hours.
remedy: As a time-honored piece of home wisdom, leftover bones simmered low and slow for most of a day, with a splash of vinegar to help draw out the good stuff, were turned into a rich broth sipped warm for comfort and easy digestion.
steps: Place leftover bones in a large pot and cover with water, adding a splash of vinegar
Bring to a gentle simmer and let it cook low for 8 to 12 hours, skimming occasionally
Strain and sip warm on its own, or use as the base for a simple soup
caution: Broth can be high in sodium if store-bought or over-salted, so those watching sodium intake should make it plain at home.
cta: Did your family ever keep a pot of bone broth going, or is this new to you? Let Grandma June know in the comments.
